business: A manufacturer of consumer packaged goods — sourcing materials, formulating, producing, testing and releasing finished product, through its own plants and through external manufacturing partners.
in_scope: Process definition, routing and recipe management
Equipment structure and physical asset management
Quality: specification, testing, deviation, non-conformance, corrective action, release
Inventory across sites and external partners

out_of_scope.owned_by: Not modelled — ISO 22716 excludes it from GMP scope

certifier: none — the practice is its own business consumer

questions_unanswered.question: Is finished output individually identified, or tracked by batch only?
questions_unanswered.consequence: Decides whether the Instances domain carries product as well as physical assets. The model must accommodate both without assuming either, so no rule may require an instance to exist and no rule may assume a lot is the finest grain.

questions_unanswered.question: What proportion of output is externally manufactured?
questions_unanswered.consequence: Where it approaches all of it, the organisation holds no production record of its own and the model is about what partners must supply rather than what plants produce.

external_standards.bears_on: Enterprise-to-plant interface, equipment hierarchy, resource models
Recipe levels and procedural structure for batch production
GMP for cosmetics — personnel, premises, equipment, materials, production, laboratory control, batch records
Food traceability — key data elements, critical tracking events, 24-hour production
Non-conformance investigation, corrective action, effectiveness verification
Electronic records, attributable entries, audit trails, electronic signatures
Trade item and location identification, two-dimensional barcodes carrying batch and serial

platform_capabilities: Audit history through change data capture
Origin and lineage tracing through the layers

resolved_questions.question: For external manufacturing, is the arrangement tolling or turnkey?
resolved_questions.answer: Turnkey. Material held at an upstream supplier or external manufacturer is theirs. Title transfers to the organisation on receipt. The organisation holds no inventory at a party it does not operate.

material_boundary.principle: The organisation masters its own composition and buys the rest.
material_boundary.statement: A purchased input may be another organisation's finished consumer product. To that organisation it is saleable output; to this one it is an ingredient or a part. What it is made from is theirs and may not be known here.
consequences: The composition graph terminates at every purchased input.
Below that terminus, hazards, certifications and origin are supplier-declared, not computed.
Recall scope below a purchased input depends on that supplier's own traceability, not on this model.
